chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the Muslim woman who is afflicted with an ailment in her body, either a fracture or a wound, in a place where it is not permissible to look at it, and the men are gentler in treating it than the women. Is it permissible for him to look at her? He said: 'When she is in need of it, so he treats her if she desires it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to look at a woman's private parts for medical treatment if she consents?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'darura' (necessity) in medical fiqh, permitting men to examine women's private areas when male physicians are more suitable and the patient consents. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing modesty (haya) with practical healthcare needs, ensuring that gender restrictions do not hinder effective treatment. The ruling underscores the importance of patient autonomy, as the permission is contingent upon the woman's willingness to be treated by a man.
